views.name: orders_enriched_with_customer
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date
FROM orders AS o
LEFT JOIN customers AS c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id

params.description: One-row-per-order enriched with customer attributes to enable queries about orders together with customer identity and location.
params.when_to_use: Retrieving order-level facts alongside customer identifiers and geographic attributes. | Filtering or grouping orders by customer attributes (city, state, zip) or by order status/timestamps. | Composing further order-level aggregations (counts, first/last timestamps, time-to-delivery) while preserving one-row-per-order grain.
params.output_schema: order_id: Order identifier at the order grain — derived from orders.order_id | customer_id: Customer identifier as recorded on the order — derived from orders.customer_id | customer_unique_id: Persistent customer identity used to link multiple orders from same buyer — derived from customers.customer_unique_id | customer_zip_code_prefix: Customer postal code prefix (geographic bucket) — derived from customers.customer_zip_code_prefix | customer_city: Customer city name — derived from customers.customer_city | customer_state: Customer state/region code — derived from customers.customer_state | order_status: Current status of the order (e.g., delivered, shipped) — derived from orders.order_status | order_purchase_timestamp: Timestamp when the order was placed — derived from orders.order_purchase_timestamp | order_approved_at: Timestamp when the order was approved — derived from orders.order_approved_at | order_delivered_carrier_date: Timestamp the order was handed to carrier — derived from orders.order_delivered_carrier_date | order_delivered_customer_date: Timestamp the order was delivered to customer — derived from orders.order_delivered_customer_date | order_estimated_delivery_date: Platform estimated delivery date for the order — derived from orders.order_estimated_delivery_date
params.grounded_columns: orders.order_id | orders.customer_id | orders.order_status | orders.order_purchase_timestamp | orders.order_approved_at | orders.order_delivered_carrier_date | orders.order_delivered_customer_date | orders.order_estimated_delivery_date | customers.customer_unique_id | customers.customer_zip_code_prefix | customers.customer_city | customers.customer_state
params.metric: This view has no aggregated measures; all outputs are raw columns projected at the order-level grain. | If you need order-level metrics derived from columns here, define them explicitly on top of this view. Examples (to be computed by a composer): | order_count = COUNT(order_id)  -- aggregate count of orders (compute after grouping) | time_to_approve = EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (order_approved_at - order_purchase_timestamp))  -- per-order duration (compute as expression per row) | time_to_deliver = EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (order_delivered_customer_date - order_purchase_timestamp))  -- per-order duration (compute as expression per row)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to 'customers' on customers.customer_id — safe because this view already LEFT JOINs customers at one-row-per-order grain; joining the base customers table by customer_id will not multiply measures beyond the view's per-order rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to 'order_payments_aggregated_by_order' on order_id — safe because that sibling view is an aggregation at order_id, producing one row per order, so joining preserves one-row-per-order and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to 'order_item_revenue_by_order' on order_id — safe because that view is aggregated by order_id; it yields one revenue summary row per order and will not duplicate this view's rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to 'latest_review_per_order' on order_id — safe because that view returns at most one review row per order (it is a RANK-based deduplication), so joining keeps one-row-per-order. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to 'orders_time_metrics' on order_id — safe when that view is windowed/aggregated to one-row-per-order; confirm sibling view grain before joining. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT directly join to one-to-many siblings such as 'order_items_with_product_and_seller' (JOIN) without first aggregating/order_id-level summarization, because order_items is one-to-many per order and would multiply this view's rows and any derived order-level measures. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT directly join to raw product or seller line-level tables that are many-per-order (via order_items) unless you aggregate those tables to order_id first (e.g., SUM(quantity), SUM(item_revenue) per order) to avoid duplicating order rows/measures. | recommendation: when combining with one-to-many datasets, either (a) aggregate the many-side to order_id before joining, or (b) use DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER based constructs on the many-side to reduce to one row per order. Always ensure the join preserves the one-row-per-order cardinality if you intend to compute order-level aggregates afterward.

views.description: Denormalized orders joined to customer attributes. Useful when analyzing orders by customer location or linking order lifecycle to customer demographic attributes. | Use for: orders by customer location (city/state/zip); order lifecycle duration by customer segment; join orders to customer-level cohorts

views.name: order_items_with_product_and_seller
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm,
  oi.seller_id,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  oi.shipping_limit_date,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value
FROM order_items AS oi
LEFT JOIN products AS p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN sellers AS s
  ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id

params.description: Provides one row per order item enriched with product attributes and seller attributes to support item-level analysis of price, freight and shipping constraints.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve item-level facts (price, freight_value, shipping_limit_date) together with product and seller attributes for reporting or further aggregation. | Compose order-level metrics by aggregating item-level measures (price, freight_value) grouped by order_id. | Filter or segment items by product attributes (category, dimensions) or seller geography (city, state, zip prefix). | Join to other single-row-per-order-item or single-row-per-order entities when building larger analytic queries (with care as described in composition).
params.output_schema: order_id: order_items.order_id — identifier of the order that contains this item (base column oi.order_id). | order_item_id: order_items.order_item_id — identifier of the specific item within the order (base column oi.order_item_id). | product_id: order_items.product_id — product identifier referenced by this order item (base column oi.product_id). | product_category_name: products.product_category_name — category name for the product (base column p.product_category_name, may be NULL if no match). | product_name_lenght: products.product_name_lenght — length of the product name as stored (base column p.product_name_lenght). | product_description_lenght: products.product_description_lenght — length of the product description as stored (base column p.product_description_lenght). | product_photos_qty: products.product_photos_qty — number of product photos as stored (base column p.product_photos_qty). | product_weight_g: products.product_weight_g — product weight in grams (base column p.product_weight_g). | product_length_cm: products.product_length_cm — product length in centimeters (base column p.product_length_cm). | product_height_cm: products.product_height_cm — product height in centimeters (base column p.product_height_cm). | product_width_cm: products.product_width_cm — product width in centimeters (base column p.product_width_cm). | seller_id: order_items.seller_id — identifier of the seller for this item (base column oi.seller_id). | seller_zip_code_prefix: sellers.seller_zip_code_prefix — seller zip code prefix (base column s.seller_zip_code_prefix, may be NULL if no match). | seller_city: sellers.seller_city — seller city (base column s.seller_city). | seller_state: sellers.seller_state — seller state (base column s.seller_state). | shipping_limit_date: order_items.shipping_limit_date — promised/latest shipping limit timestamp for this item (base column oi.shipping_limit_date). | price: order_items.price — item price charged for this item (base column oi.price). | freight_value: order_items.freight_value — shipping/freight charged for this item (base column oi.freight_value).
params.grounded_columns: order_items.order_id | order_items.order_item_id | order_items.product_id | order_items.seller_id | order_items.shipping_limit_date | order_items.price | order_items.freight_value | products.product_id | products.product_category_name | products.product_name_lenght | products.product_description_lenght | products.product_photos_qty | products.product_weight_g | products.product_length_cm | products.product_height_cm | products.product_width_cm | sellers.seller_id | sellers.seller_zip_code_prefix | sellers.seller_city | sellers.seller_state
params.metric: price = order_items.price (atomic numeric measure stored per order item) | freight_value = order_items.freight_value (atomic numeric measure stored per order item) | item_revenue (not materialized in view) = SUM(price) aggregated over groupings of order_id/order_item_id or larger grains — when aggregating, sum price at the order_item grain to avoid double-counting. | order_level_total_price (not materialized) = SUM(price) GROUP BY order_id — derive by aggregating this view's price over order_id. | order_level_total_freight (not materialized) = SUM(freight_value) GROUP BY order_id — derive by aggregating this view's freight_value over order_id.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_enriched_with_customer on order_id — safe because orders_enriched_with_customer is one-row-per-order (same or coarser grain). Joining on order_id will not duplicate item-level measures; it simply repeats order-level attributes across the multiple order_items for that order. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_physical_dimensions_and_volume on product_id — safe if that view is one-row-per-product (coarser grain). Joining preserves the one-row-per-order-item grain and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_category_translation_lookup on product_category_name — safe when that lookup is one-row-per-category; it enriches category attributes without duplicating item measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to seller_location_geocode_candidates on seller_id — safe if that view is one-row-per-seller or has been de-duplicated to one row per seller; it will not multiply item measures. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT directly join to one-to-many tables or views (for example, a hypothetical table of seller_contact_numbers with multiple phone rows per seller, or a reviews table with multiple reviews per order_item) without first aggregating or deduplicating those sources to one row per join key. Such joins would multiply rows for the same order_item and thus duplicate price and freight_value. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT join to order_payments_aggregated_by_order without understanding its grain — because that view is aggregated to the order grain, joining it to this order-item-grain view is safe only when the payments view is strictly one-row-per-order. If order_payments_aggregated_by_order contains multiple rows per order (e.g., one per payment_type), join would multiply item measures; instead aggregate payments to one row per order (e.g., SUM(payment_value) GROUP BY order_id) before joining. | aggregation guidance: when composing higher-level metrics (order-level totals, customer-level spend), always aggregate price and freight_value at this view's grain (order_id, order_item_id) before joining to any many-side dimension to avoid double counting. | join key summary: safe one-to-many directions are (this view many order_items) -> (one orders_enriched_with_customer per order_id), (one product row per product_id), (one seller row per seller_id). Avoid many-to-many joins that create multiplicative effects without explicit aggregation.

views.description: Order items enriched with product attributes and seller location. Useful for item-level revenue, shipping, and product category analysis while preserving join keys for aggregations. | Use for: item-level revenue and freight analysis; product category sales by seller location; shipping SLA or delay analysis per item

views.name: order_payments_aggregated_by_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_segments_count,
  SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_total
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY order_id

params.description: Per-order aggregates of payment segments: number of payment segments and total payment value per order.
params.when_to_use: Get payment-level summary metrics per order (e.g., total paid and count of payment segments) for reporting or to join to order-level data. | Compose into higher-level queries that need order-level payment metrics (e.g., revenue by customer, refunds analysis) while preserving correct aggregation. | Filter or rank orders by payment totals or number of payment segments before joining to other order-level datasets.
params.output_schema: order_id: the unique identifier of the order; derived from order_payments.order_id (GROUP BY key). | payment_segments_count: the count of payment segments/rows from order_payments for this order; derived from COUNT(*) over order_payments grouped by order_id. | payment_value_total: the sum of payment_value for this order; derived from SUM(payment_value) over order_payments grouped by order_id.
params.metric: payment_segments_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of order_payments rows per order_id | payment_value_total = SUM(payment_value)  -- sum of order_payments.payment_value per order_id
params.composition: Join safely to order-level one-row-per-order views/tables: e.g., join to orders_enriched_with_customer on order_id — safe because orders_enriched_with_customer is one row per order_id so this AGG's measures are not duplicated. | Join safely to other one-row-per-order aggregates (e.g., order_item_revenue_by_order) on order_id — safe because both sides are aggregated to the same grain (order_id); measures can be combined or used together without re-aggregation. | Do NOT directly join to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., order_items_with_product_and_seller, latest_review_per_order if it can be many, seller_location_geocode_candidates when multiple candidates exist) without re-aggregating the many-side first — such joins would multiply rows and thereby duplicate payment_segments_count and payment_value_total. Instead, either: | - aggregate the many-side to order_id before joining, or | - join at order_id and then re-aggregate (e.g., SUM(payment_value_total) over order_id) after the join to restore correct totals. | When composing with windowed or rank-based sibling views (orders_time_metrics, latest_review_per_order), ensure those views are one-row-per-order before joining. If they are not guaranteed one-row-per-order, reduce them to one row per order (e.g., pick latest or aggregate) to avoid duplicating this view's measures. | Normalization (lookup) tables (e.g., product_category_translation_lookup, products_physical_dimensions_and_volume) should only be joined if first correlated to an order-level key or pre-aggregated to order_id; direct joins on product/seller keys (one-to-many from orders) will cause measure duplication.

views.description: Aggregated payment metrics per order: total payment amount and count of payment segments. Useful to reconcile order-level revenue and detect split payments. | Use for: compare payment_value_total to order_items revenue; identify orders with multiple payment segments; average payment segments per order across time

views.name: order_item_revenue_by_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  SUM(price) AS items_price_total,
  SUM(freight_value) AS items_freight_total,
  COUNT(*) AS items_count
FROM order_items
GROUP BY order_id

params.description: Per-order aggregated totals for item price, item freight, and item count (one row per order_id).
params.when_to_use: Get total item price, total item freight, and number of items for a specific order or set of orders. | Join order-level item totals into order header data (e.g., to compute order-level revenue or margins). | Compose higher-level metrics per customer, seller, date range, or other dimensions by joining and then aggregating these per-order measures. | Filter or rank orders by items_price_total, items_freight_total, or items_count.
params.output_schema: order_id: identifier for the order; comes from order_items.order_id (grouping key). | items_price_total: SUM(price) aggregated per order; derives from order_items.price. | items_freight_total: SUM(freight_value) aggregated per order; derives from order_items.freight_value. | items_count: COUNT(*) of order_items rows per order; counts order_items rows (one row per item).
params.metric: items_price_total = SUM(order_items.price)  -- sum of price over all items with same order_id | items_freight_total = SUM(order_items.freight_value)  -- sum of freight_value over all items with same order_id | items_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of order_items rows per order_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_enriched_with_customer on order_id — safe because orders_enriched_with_customer is one-row-per-order (JOIN will not duplicate this view's measures). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to order_payments_aggregated_by_order on order_id — safe because that view is also aggregated per order_id (one-row-per-order), so measures remain aligned and not multiplied. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_review_per_order on order_id — safe because latest_review_per_order is one-row-per-order (ranked to single row per order), so joining preserves this view's one-row-per-order semantics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_time_metrics on order_id or order date (if orders_time_metrics is one-row-per-order or per-order-time bucket) — only safe if orders_time_metrics is one-row-per-order; verify that ordering/windowing produced one row per order before joining. | DO NOT join directly to order_items (base table) without re-aggregation: joining this aggregated view back to order_items (one-to-many from order to items) will multiply items_price_total, items_freight_total, and items_count for each matching item row. | DO NOT join to order_items_with_product_and_seller (JOIN) without re-aggregation: that view likely contains one row per order item (or more if it expands by product/seller), so joining it directly will duplicate the aggregated measures unless you re-aggregate after joining. | DO NOT join to sibling views that are one-to-many relative to order_id (for example, any per-item or per-product expanded view) without first aggregating those siblings to one-row-per-order; otherwise this view's measures will be multiplied. | When composing higher-level aggregations (e.g., totals per customer, per-seller, per-day): join this view to the dimension keyed by order_id (or to an orders-level view keyed by order_id) and then aggregate the items_price_total, items_freight_total, and items_count (use SUM on these columns). This preserves correctness because this view is one-row-per-order.

views.description: Order-level aggregation of item financials: total items price, total freight, item count. Use to compute order revenue from items for revenue reconciliation and per-order metrics. | Use for: order revenue calculations; average items per order; freight contribution to order value

views.name: latest_review_per_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.review_id,
  r.order_id,
  r.review_score,
  r.review_comment_title,
  r.review_comment_message,
  r.review_creation_date,
  r.review_answer_timestamp,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.order_id ORDER BY r.review_creation_date DESC, r.review_id) AS review_rank_by_order
FROM order_reviews AS r

params.description: Latest review row per order (ranked reviews per order) showing the most recent reviews and their metadata.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the most-recent (or top-N by rank) review(s) for each order. | Compose queries that need one review record per order (e.g., join latest review to order-level metrics). | Filter orders by having a latest review meeting criteria (score, keywords, answered/unanswered). | Build aggregates over latest-per-order reviews (e.g., average latest review score by seller or date) without double-counting multiple reviews per order.
params.output_schema: review_id: unique identifier of the review — from order_reviews.review_id | order_id: identifier of the order this review is for — from order_reviews.order_id | review_score: numeric score given in the review — from order_reviews.review_score | review_comment_title: short title/summary of the review comment — from order_reviews.review_comment_title | review_comment_message: full review comment text — from order_reviews.review_comment_message | review_creation_date: timestamp when the review was created — from order_reviews.review_creation_date | review_answer_timestamp: timestamp when the review was answered (if answered) — from order_reviews.review_answer_timestamp | review_rank_by_order: integer rank (1 = newest) of this review within the same order, computed as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY review_creation_date DESC, review_id) — synthetic/derived in the view
params.grounded_columns: order_reviews.review_id | order_reviews.order_id | order_reviews.review_score | order_reviews.review_comment_title | order_reviews.review_comment_message | order_reviews.review_creation_date | order_reviews.review_answer_timestamp
params.metric: review_rank_by_order = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY order_reviews.order_id ORDER BY order_reviews.review_creation_date DESC, order_reviews.review_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_enriched_with_customer on latest_review_per_order.order_id = orders_enriched_with_customer.order_id — safe because latest_review_per_order has at most one (and typically one) row per review_id and ranks are per order; joining on order_id will not duplicate review-level measures only if you restrict latest_review_per_order to the desired rank (e.g., WHERE review_rank_by_order = 1). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to order_payments_aggregated_by_order on latest_review_per_order.order_id = order_payments_aggregated_by_order.order_id — safe because order_payments_aggregated_by_order is aggregated to one row per order; when you join after filtering latest_review_per_order to one row per order, measures (e.g., payment totals) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to order_item_revenue_by_order on latest_review_per_order.order_id = order_item_revenue_by_order.order_id — safe for the same reason as payments: that sibling view is aggregated to one row per order; do not join without ensuring latest_review_per_order is limited to one row per order. | do NOT join directly to order_items_with_product_and_seller (JOIN) without re-aggregation: order_items_with_product_and_seller is one-to-many per order (multiple items per order). Joining latest_review_per_order (one row per review) to that table will multiply review rows by the number of items, thereby duplicating any review-level measures. If you need order-item details together with the latest review, either (a) aggregate order_items_with_product_and_seller to order-level first, or (b) join and then re-aggregate, being mindful to use appropriate aggregations (e.g., SUM, AVG) and GROUP BY review_id/order_id. | do NOT join to sibling JOIN views that are one-to-many (e.g., seller_location_geocode_candidates may be one-to-many per seller) unless you deduplicate or aggregate the target to one row per join key first. | safe composition pattern: first filter this view to the single row per order you need (e.g., WHERE review_rank_by_order = 1), then join to any dimension or order-aggregated view on order_id (or to customer dimension via orders_enriched_with_customer) — this preserves cardinality and prevents measure duplication. | note on rank semantics: this view exposes the rank but does not itself filter to rank = 1. Any composition that requires exactly one review per order should explicitly filter review_rank_by_order = 1 before joining to one-to-many targets or before aggregating across orders.

views.description: For orders with multiple reviews, keep the latest review by review_creation_date. Exposes review rank and can be used to filter the most recent review per order. | Use for: select latest review per order; analyze latest review sentiment or score per order; count orders with at least one review (review_rank_by_order = 1)

views.name: orders_time_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  -- differences in seconds where possible; timestamps are text so use julianday()
  (CASE WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND o.order_approved_at IS NOT NULL THEN
     (julianday(o.order_approved_at) - julianday(o.order_purchase_timestamp)) * 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0
   END) AS seconds_purchase_to_approved,
  (CASE WHEN o.order_approved_at IS NOT NULL AND o.order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL THEN
     (julianday(o.order_delivered_carrier_date) - julianday(o.order_approved_at)) * 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0
   END) AS seconds_approved_to_carrier,
  (CASE WHEN o.order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL THEN
     (julianday(o.order_delivered_customer_date) - julianday(o.order_delivered_carrier_date)) * 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0
   END) AS seconds_carrier_to_customer
FROM orders AS o

params.description: Per-order timing metrics: time intervals (in seconds) between key order timestamp events (purchase → approved → carrier → customer).
params.when_to_use: Calculate per-order latency intervals between order events (purchase to approved, approved to carrier, carrier to customer). | Aggregate order-level lead times (e.g., average seconds from purchase to delivery) by customer, seller, date, or other dimensions after appropriate grouping. | Filter or segment orders by timing (e.g., orders with approval delays > X seconds) before joining to other order-level data.
params.output_schema: order_id: unique identifier for the order; sourced from orders.order_id | order_purchase_timestamp: original purchase timestamp for the order (text); sourced from orders.order_purchase_timestamp | order_approved_at: original approval timestamp for the order (text); sourced from orders.order_approved_at | order_delivered_carrier_date: timestamp when the order was handed to carrier (text); sourced from orders.order_delivered_carrier_date | order_delivered_customer_date: timestamp when the order was delivered to customer (text); sourced from orders.order_delivered_customer_date | seconds_purchase_to_approved: numeric seconds between order_purchase_timestamp and order_approved_at when both present; computed from julianday(order_approved_at) - julianday(order_purchase_timestamp) * 86400 | seconds_approved_to_carrier: numeric seconds between order_approved_at and order_delivered_carrier_date when both present; computed from julianday(order_delivered_carrier_date) - julianday(order_approved_at) * 86400 | seconds_carrier_to_customer: numeric seconds between order_delivered_carrier_date and order_delivered_customer_date when both present; computed from julianday(order_delivered_customer_date) - julianday(order_delivered_carrier_date) * 86400
params.metric: seconds_purchase_to_approved = CASE WHEN orders.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND orders.order_approved_at IS NOT NULL THEN (julianday(orders.order_approved_at) - julianday(orders.order_purchase_timestamp)) * 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0 END | seconds_approved_to_carrier = CASE WHEN orders.order_approved_at IS NOT NULL AND orders.order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL THEN (julianday(orders.order_delivered_carrier_date) - julianday(orders.order_approved_at)) * 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0 END | seconds_carrier_to_customer = CASE WHEN orders.order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL AND orders.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL THEN (julianday(orders.order_delivered_customer_date) - julianday(orders.order_delivered_carrier_date)) * 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0 END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any table or view that is one-row-per-order on order_id (for example, order_payments_aggregated_by_order and order_item_revenue_by_order) using orders_time_metrics.order_id = <other>.order_id — safe because orders_time_metrics has exactly one row per order_id (the view's declared grain), so measures (the seconds_... columns) will not be duplicated. | Safe to join to orders_enriched_with_customer on order_id when that view is also one-row-per-order (JOIN on order_id) because both sides are order-level and will not multiply rows. | Do NOT directly join orders_time_metrics to one-to-many tables/views such as order_items_with_product_and_seller (order items) or seller_location_geocode_candidates (if it contains multiple candidates per seller) without first aggregating the many-side back to order-level (for example, SUM, AVG, or MAX per order_id) or joining through an intermediate one-row-per-order view. Direct joins to one-to-many relationships will multiply rows and incorrectly duplicate the seconds_* measures. | If you need to combine with order_items_with_product_and_seller to compute item-weighted or item-count-normalized timing metrics, first aggregate the item table to order-level (e.g., SUM(quantity) or AVG(metric) GROUP BY order_id) and then join that aggregated result to this view on order_id. | When joining to latest_review_per_order (which is one-row-per-order by name), it is safe on order_id; when joining to rank-based or normalized lookup tables (product_category_translation_lookup, products_physical_dimensions_and_volume), ensure those lookups are reduced to one-row-per-order (via their join keys) before joining, otherwise re-aggregate after the join to avoid multiplying timing metrics.

views.description: Order-level computed time intervals between lifecycle timestamps (purchase->approved, approved->delivered to carrier, carrier->customer). Useful for SLA, delivery time analysis and as features for modeling. | Use for: delivery time SLA and bottleneck analysis; median/average time between lifecycle events; identify outlier slow deliveries

views.name: product_category_translation_lookup

params.description: Lookup of product category display name and its English translation, at the granularity of a product category name.
params.when_to_use: Translate or normalize product category names to English for reporting or joining when grouping by product_category_name | Enrich product or order item data with an English product category label when the source has product_category_name | Build user-facing reports or downstream aggregated metrics that need a stable English category label per product_category_name
params.output_schema: product_category_name: product category name in source language — derived from product_category_name_translation.product_category_name | product_category_name_english: English translation/normalized label for the product category — derived from product_category_name_translation.product_category_name_english
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a fact or dimension that has product_category_name as a foreign/key field using an equality join on product_category_name — safe because this view is one-row-per-product_category_name (NORM) so joining on that key will not duplicate this view's columns (it will at most add the English label to each matching fact row). Example: JOIN order_items_with_product_and_seller ON order_items_with_product_and_seller.product_category_name = product_category_translation_lookup.product_category_name — safe because the lookup is one row per product_category_name. | do NOT join this view to a one-to-many child of product_category_name without re-aggregating the child first, because that would multiply rows/metrics that are expected to be one-per-product_category_name. For example, do not join product_category_translation_lookup directly to a table that lists multiple product SKUs per product_category_name and then sum metrics from the lookup side without aggregating the SKU-level rows first. | when composing aggregates: if you aggregate metrics from a many-side (e.g., order_items) and also want the English label, perform the aggregation on the many-side grouped by product_category_name, then join the aggregated result to this lookup on product_category_name. This preserves correct cardinality (one aggregated row per product_category_name) and prevents double-counting. | safe to join from this view (as lookup) to any table keyed by product_category_name. Not safe to treat this view as an additive metric source — it contains only descriptive columns (no numeric measures) and should be used to annotate or group by product_category_name rather than to aggregate numeric measures without proper grouping/aggregation on the other side.

views.description: Canonical lookup for product category English name. Use to join product categories to human-readable English labels. | Use for: map product_category_name to English label; group product metrics by translated category

views.name: products_physical_dimensions_and_volume
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_category_name,
  product_name_lenght,
  product_description_lenght,
  product_photos_qty,
  product_weight_g,
  product_length_cm,
  product_height_cm,
  product_width_cm,
  (product_length_cm * product_height_cm * product_width_cm) AS product_volume_cm3,
  (CASE WHEN product_length_cm IS NULL OR product_height_cm IS NULL OR product_width_cm IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_dimension_flag
FROM products

params.description: Provides per-product physical attributes and computed volume, indicating missing dimension data.
params.when_to_use: Report product physical specs (weight, length, height, width) and computed volume per product_id | Filter or identify products missing one or more physical dimensions | Compose product-level joins where a single row per product is required (e.g., enrich products with category names or aggregate product metrics) | Seed aggregations by product (e.g., combine with sales/orders aggregated by product_id)
params.output_schema: product_id: unique identifier for the product — sourced from products.product_id | product_category_name: product category descriptive name — sourced from products.product_category_name | product_name_lenght: length (character count) of the product name as stored — sourced from products.product_name_lenght | product_description_lenght: length (character count) of the product description as stored — sourced from products.product_description_lenght | product_photos_qty: number of product photos associated with the product — sourced from products.product_photos_qty | product_weight_g: product weight in grams — sourced from products.product_weight_g | product_length_cm: product length in centimeters — sourced from products.product_length_cm | product_height_cm: product height in centimeters — sourced from products.product_height_cm | product_width_cm: product width in centimeters — sourced from products.product_width_cm | product_volume_cm3: computed product volume in cubic centimeters = product_length_cm * product_height_cm * product_width_cm — derived expression using products.product_length_cm, products.product_height_cm, products.product_width_cm | missing_dimension_flag: indicator (1/0) that at least one of length/height/width is NULL; 1 = missing at least one dimension, 0 = all three present — derived from products.product_length_cm, products.product_height_cm, products.product_width_cm
params.grounded_columns: products.product_id | products.product_category_name | products.product_name_lenght | products.product_description_lenght | products.product_photos_qty | products.product_weight_g | products.product_length_cm | products.product_height_cm | products.product_width_cm
params.metric: product_volume_cm3 = product_length_cm * product_height_cm * product_width_cm | missing_dimension_flag = CASE WHEN product_length_cm IS NULL OR product_height_cm IS NULL OR product_width_cm IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/lookups that are one-row-per-product or one-row-per-product_id — e.g., product_category_translation_lookup on product_category_name (or on product_category key if you expose it) — safe because this view is one-row-per product_id and the lookup is keyed 1:1, so measures (volume, flags) are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_enriched_with_customer or order_items_with_product_and_seller only after aggregating those tables to product_id (e.g., sum(quantity) or sum(revenue) grouped by product_id). This view is one-row-per product_id; joining it directly to raw order_items (which is many order_items per product) would multiply product rows and duplicate per-product measures. | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many table/view (orders, order_items_with_product_and_seller, latest_review_per_order, seller_location_geocode_candidates if multiple candidates per seller, etc.) without first aggregating or deduplicating the many-side to product_id. Direct joins to many-side sources will multiply rows and therefore duplicate computed measures such as product_volume_cm3 and will break correctness of downstream aggregations. | safe composition pattern for analytics: to compute product-level KPIs combining sales and dimensions, first aggregate sales (order_items) to product_id (e.g., total_qty, total_revenue), then INNER JOIN or LEFT JOIN this view on product_id. Because products_physical_dimensions_and_volume has one row per product_id, the join will not duplicate the aggregated sales metrics. | if you need to join by product_category_name to a category-level source that can be many-to-one (multiple categories mapping to same name or translations), ensure the category side is deduplicated or use an aggregated/lookup-normalized category view to maintain cardinality safety.

views.description: Projection of products with derived physical volume (cm^3) and a flag for missing critical dimensions. Helpful for shipping cost modeling and dimensional analysis. | Use for: identify heavy or large products by volume/weight; filter products missing dimensions; derive shipping dimensional weight features

views.name: seller_location_geocode_candidates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.seller_id,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  g.geolocation_lat,
  g.geolocation_lng,
  g.geolocation_city,
  g.geolocation_state
FROM sellers AS s
LEFT JOIN geolocation AS g
  ON s.seller_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix

params.description: Provides candidate geocoded locations for sellers by linking sellers (by zip prefix) to geolocation records (lat/lng and city/state) — useful for mapping or spatial joins at the seller + geolocation coordinate grain.
params.when_to_use: Find geographic coordinates for sellers (approximate by seller_zip_code_prefix) for mapping, distance calculations, or spatial joins. | Join seller attributes (city/state/zip prefix) to geolocation coordinates when composing order-level or product-level analyses that need seller location. | Serve as the base for deriving seller-level spatial metrics (e.g., distance from customer, clustering of sellers) after de-duplicating or aggregating as required.
params.output_schema: seller_id: unique identifier for the seller — derives from sellers.seller_id | seller_zip_code_prefix: seller's zip code prefix — derives from sellers.seller_zip_code_prefix | seller_city: seller's reported city — derives from sellers.seller_city | seller_state: seller's reported state — derives from sellers.seller_state | geolocation_lat: latitude coordinate from matched geolocation record — derives from geolocation.geolocation_lat | geolocation_lng: longitude coordinate from matched geolocation record — derives from geolocation.geolocation_lng | geolocation_city: city name from matched geolocation record — derives from geolocation.geolocation_city | geolocation_state: state name from matched geolocation record — derives from geolocation.geolocation_state
params.grounded_columns: sellers.seller_id | sellers.seller_zip_code_prefix | sellers.seller_city | sellers.seller_state | geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_prefix | geolocation.geolocation_lat | geolocation.geolocation_lng | geolocation.geolocation_city | geolocation.geolocation_state
params.metric: No aggregated measures are produced by this view. All output columns are passthrough columns from base tables (no derived aggregate expressions).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like, one-row-per-seller objects (for example, any view/table that has seller_id as a unique key) on seller_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-seller_id (grain = [seller_id, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng]) and will not duplicate measures when the other side is one-row-per-seller. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to seller-level aggregated metrics (e.g., an aggregation of orders or order_items grouped by seller_id) on seller_id — safe because the aggregation already produces one row per seller_id, avoiding multiplication of rows. Example: join orders_enriched_with_customer aggregated by seller_id. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed by seller_id without re-aggregation (e.g., raw order_items, orders, or any order_items_with_product_and_seller view that is one-to-many per seller) because that will multiply seller rows by the number of related child rows and thereby duplicate any seller-level measures or lead to row explosion. If you need to combine with one-to-many data, first aggregate the child data to the seller_id level (or to this view's grain) before joining. | do NOT assume uniqueness when joining on seller_zip_code_prefix to the geolocation table in reverse: geolocation may contain multiple geolocation rows per geolocation_zip_code_prefix (e.g., multiple coordinate candidates). This view's LEFT JOIN will produce multiple rows per seller_id if geolocation has multiple matches; consumers must handle deduplication (for example, pick the first/closest/aggregated coordinate) if a single coordinate per seller is required. | When composing spatial metrics (distances, bounding-box counts, clustering), ensure joins preserve the intended grain: treat this view as representing candidate seller-location rows (grain = seller_id + geolocation_lat + geolocation_lng). If you need exactly one row per seller, either filter to a single geolocation candidate per seller (via ranking/deduplication) or aggregate coordinates appropriately prior to downstream joins. | Safe join keys examples: join to products or product_category_translation_lookup via seller_id only if those tables are one-row-per-seller or pre-aggregated to seller_id; join to order-level aggregates (e.g., order_payments_aggregated_by_order aggregated up to seller) only after grouping to seller_id to avoid duplication.

views.description: Join sellers to geolocation points by zip code prefix to provide latitude/longitude candidates for seller locations. Useful for mapping and distance calculations; note there may be multiple geolocation rows per zip prefix. | Use for: map sellers on a map using geolocation points; disambiguate multiple geolocation points per zip prefix; compute distances from customers to sellers after joining customer geocodes

views.name: products_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  COALESCE(t.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS product_category_name,
  p.product_name_lenght AS product_name_length,
  p.product_description_lenght AS product_description_length,
  p.product_photos_qty AS product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g AS product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm AS product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm AS product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm AS product_width_cm
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t
  ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
views.description: Canonicalized product attributes and category for each product_id. Normalizes product category name and exposes size/weight/volume dimensions for joins and aggregation.

views.name: order_items_detailed
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  oi.shipping_limit_date,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value
FROM order_items oi
views.description: Order-item level sales lines with prices, freight, seller and order references. One row per order_id + order_item_id containing product and seller ids and monetary measures.

views.name: orders_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date
FROM orders_enriched_with_customer o
views.description: Basic order header information with purchase and delivery timestamps and order status. Exposes order_id and purchase date for deriving daily sales time series.

views.name: delivered_orders_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  orders.order_id,
  orders.customer_id,
  orders.order_status,
  orders.order_purchase_timestamp,
  orders.order_approved_at,
  orders.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  orders.order_delivered_customer_date,
  orders.order_estimated_delivery_date
FROM orders
WHERE orders.order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: One row per order that was actually delivered. Keeps core order attributes for delivered orders to be reused by joins and aggregations (purchase/approved/delivered timestamps and order status).

views.name: order_payments_per_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  SUM(payment_value) AS payment_total_value,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  MAX(payment_installments) AS payment_max_installments
FROM
  order_payments
GROUP BY
  order_id
grain: order_id  -- one row per order with aggregated payment metrics
views.description: Aggregate payments per order: sums payment_value and exposes payment-level details grouped to order granularity. Keeps payment installments/type info aggregated as needed for downstream monetary calculations.

views.name: customer_delivered_order_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oec.customer_id,
  oec.customer_unique_id,
  MAX(oec.order_purchase_timestamp) AS recency_latest_order_ts,
  -- recency_days_from_reference left as days difference from max(order_purchase_timestamp) to date('now')
  CAST((julianday(date('now')) - julianday(date(MAX(oec.order_purchase_timestamp)))) AS INTEGER) AS recency_days_from_reference,
  COUNT(DISTINCT oec.order_id) AS frequency_orders,
  SUM(op.payment_value) AS monetary_total
FROM
  orders_enriched_with_customer AS oec
JOIN
  order_payments AS op
  ON oec.order_id = op.order_id
WHERE
  oec.order_status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY
  oec.customer_unique_id,
  oec.customer_id
grain: customer_unique_id  -- one row per customer (considering only delivered orders)

semantic_filters.only_customers_with_delivered_orders: true  -- this view excludes customers with zero delivered orders

views.description: Per-customer (customer_id and customer_unique_id) metrics computed from delivered orders: recency (latest purchase timestamp), frequency (# delivered orders), monetary (sum of order payments). Exposes required keys and raw measures for scoring and further segmentation.

views.name: orders_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  orders.order_id AS order_id,
  orders.customer_id AS customer_id,
  datetime(orders.order_purchase_timestamp) AS order_purchase_timestamp
FROM orders
views.description: Canonical per-order attributes needed for customer-level lifecycle and joins: order id, customer id, and normalized purchase timestamp (as datetime).

views.name: order_payments_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_rows_count
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_value IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY order_id
views.description: Aggregated payment measures per order: sum of payment_value and count of payment rows. Keeps order_id as key so it can be joined to orders and customers.

views.name: customer_orders_timings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customer_id AS customer_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count,
  MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_order_purchase_ts,
  MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_order_purchase_ts
FROM orders_enriched_with_customer o
GROUP BY o.customer_id
views.description: Per-customer order-level aggregates useful for lifecycle and counts: order_count, earliest and latest order_purchase_timestamp, and (optionally) sum of order payments by joining order_payments_agg. This view exposes raw aggregates; final query computes avg payment per order and lifespan in weeks.
